legend: Christoph Clavius, Astrolabium (1593), Book II, Proposition VI, p. 419. Public domain, via Archive.org, scan by University of Michigan
After Ferdinand Magellan's expedition, it became clear to everyone in Europe what scholars and the ancient Greeks had known for a long time: the Earth was, indeed, not a disc.

Less well known is that, around the same time, European scholars were working on a much more ambitious theory of the motion of the celestial bodies. Astronomers often described planetary motion using deferents and epicycles, circles whose centres themselves moved along other circles. Some scholars took this idea further and hypothesized that a system of circular orbits was stable precisely when the centre of every orbit lay on another orbit in the same system.
Today we know that celestial mechanics are somewhat more complicated than that.

From their observations, the scholars calculated the radii of the circles needed for their model, but not their positions. Therefore, they wanted to know whether these circles could be arranged in a stable manner, that is, so that the centre of every circle lies on the circumference of another circle.
Checking all possible arrangements by hand was rather inconvenient, but fortunately, we now have computers to determine whether such an arrangement is possible.
A stable arrangement for the third sample. Each dot marks the centre of the circle with the corresponding colour.
input: One line with an integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2\leq n\leq {2 \cdot 10^5}$$$), the number of radii.
One line with $$$n$$$ integers $$$r$$$ ($$$1\le r\le {10^9}$$$), the radius of each circle.
output: If it is possible to arrange the circles in a stable manner, output "possible". Otherwise, output "impossible".

legend.ai: Christoph Clavius，《Astrolabium》（1593），第二卷，命题 VI，第419页。公有领域，来自 Archive.org，由密歇根大学扫描。
费迪南德·麦哲伦的远征之后，欧洲所有人都明白了学者和古希腊人早已知道的事情：地球确实不是一个圆盘。
较少为人所知的是，大约在同一时期，欧洲学者正在研究一种更为宏大的天体运动理论。天文学家常用均轮和本轮来描述行星运动：这些圆的圆心本身沿着其他圆运动。一些学者进一步发展了这一想法，并假设，当且仅当每个轨道的圆心都位于同一系统中的另一条轨道上时，圆形轨道系统才是稳定的。
如今我们知道，天体力学比那要复杂一些。
根据观测结果，学者们计算出了模型所需圆的半径，但没有确定它们的位置。因此，他们想知道这些圆能否以稳定的方式排列，也就是说，每个圆的圆心都位于另一个圆的圆周上。
手动检查所有可能的排列相当不方便，但幸运的是，我们现在有计算机可以判断这样的排列是否存在。
第三个样例的一种稳定排列。每个点表示相应颜色圆的圆心。

input.ai: 一行包含一个整数 $$$n$$$($$$2\leq n\leq {2 \cdot 10^5}$$$)，表示半径的数量。
一行包含 $$$n$$$ 个整数 $$$r$$$($$$1\le r\le {10^9}$$$)，表示每个圆的半径。

output.ai: 如果可以将这些圆稳定地排列，输出“possible”；否则，输出“impossible”。
